findings.desc: .lattice/story/actives/B-7dff/checklist.json:387 CHK-004 title promises to Prove parallel equals serial on the real plan and record the measured makespan, and its context/DoneWhen say the makespan must surface so the 3.17x claim is checkable rather than asserted / no hardcoded 3.17x. The delivered, gate-enforced regression (packages/main/src/tasks/validate-parallel-equivalence-smoke.ts:30-35, npm run test:validate-parallel-equivalence) deliberately never runs the real ~104-command validate plan (comment: real plan takes 10-18 minutes per mode ... would make validate recursive); it only measures a synthetic 6-command fixture with 700ms probes, so the printed serial=/parallel=/speedup= line is disconnected from the workload the 3.17x claim describes (dominated by one ~267s command). No mechanical/repeatable command anywhere in this story ever measures jobs=1 vs jobs=4 wall time on the real, fully-declared plan: the only jobs=1 runs on the real plan (CHK-003:happy:0 evidence) checked commands[] order equivalence, not timing; every other real-plan timing pair cited in CHK-004:happy:0 and CHK-005:happy:0 evidence notes (781.3s/611.6s and 1006.4s/634.9s) is jobs=4 vs jobs=4 (declaration-coverage effect, not scheduler-vs-serial effect), captured as one-off manual validate --json runs rather than a reusable test. So the headline speedup claim that motivated this story is not covered by any evidence a future run can mechanically re-verify. Recommend either widening the smoke to at least assert a real-plan jobs=1-vs-jobs=4 timing check (even a coarse threshold), or explicitly re-scoping CHK-004s DoneWhen to state the real-plan number is manual/one-off and not gate-enforced.

packages/main/src/core/validation-executor.ts:266-298,398-447 (readGitStatus/detectNewDirtyStatus inside runValidationCommand): the worktree-pollution side-effect probe takes a REPO-WIDE git-status snapshot before/after each command, and CHK-003 moved execution onto the concurrent scheduler (jobs=4 default) without scoping this probe per-command. When two commands run concurrently and one of them dirties the tree, any OTHER concurrently-running command whose before/after window straddles that write gets falsely blamed too, because detectNewDirtyStatus only compares against its OWN before-snapshot, which is repo-wide, not scoped to files that command touched. Reproduced directly against the built dist: a plan with dirtying-A (writes accidental-a.txt after 300ms) and clean-B (pure sleep, no writes) both declaring the same shared git-common-dir claim, run at jobs=2, reports worktreePollution on BOTH commands (clean-B: paths=[\"accidental-a.txt\"], blocking=true) even though clean-B never touched the filesystem. The identical plan at jobs=1 (serial, pre-B-7dff behaviour) correctly attributes the pollution to dirtying-A only and reports null pollution for clean-B. This corrupts gate-consumed per-command evidence (result.commands[i].worktreePollution, which formatWorktreePollutionDetails/evaluateDirtyGate feed into allPass and into process-events.jsonl audit lines) by falsely failing/blaming innocent commands whenever ANY concurrently-scheduled command dirties the tree — misleading root-cause diagnosis and potentially failing commands that did nothing wrong. Since lattice.config.json now declares git-common-dir:shared on ~90 of 104 commands (CHK-005), this is a realistic, not theoretical, concurrency window. No test in validate-plan-scheduling.test.mjs or validate-resource-claims.test.mjs exercises pollution attribution under concurrency.

doc-code-drift: packages/main/src/tasks/validate-command-timeout-smoke.ts:21 top-of-file docstring still claims check 12 verifies 'validation-executor.ts and verifier.ts remain byte-for-byte unmodified from main (git diff, soft-skip on environment failure)'. This story (B-7dff) intentionally rewrote check 12 itself (lines ~362-386) to a different, weaker invariant (no copy of resolvePinnedCommandTimeoutMs matching logic in either file) precisely because B-7dff must modify both validation-executor.ts and verifier.ts. The file's own summary docstring was not updated to match, so a future reader relying on the top-of-file summary would believe a stronger byte-identity guarantee still holds when it no longer does.

maintainability: packages/main/src/core/validation-executor.ts:733 (inside resolveValidationCommandResources) and :754 (inside resolveValidationPlanEntries) independently re-derive the same 'this command declared nothing so it gets the fail-closed exclusive default' condition (claims.length === 0 after mapping vs. !(Array.isArray(command.resources) && command.resources.length > 0)). The two expressions are equivalent today only by inspection; resolveValidationCommandResources never returns whether it applied the default, so resolveValidationPlanEntries has to recompute the same rule from the raw field. If the declaredness rule ever changes (e.g. to also treat an all-invalid-but-nonempty resources array as undeclared), the two call sites can silently diverge and exclusiveByDefault/the printed declared= count would stop matching what the scheduler actually enforced.

packages/main/src/handlers/verifier.ts:977-1006,1318-1328,891-893 — F-003s own detection-not-lost promise is broken in the real persisted-evidence path. executeValidationPlan (validation-executor.ts) correctly sets result.concurrentWorktreePollution when pollution cannot be attributed to one command, and the plan-level status/allPass correctly fail. But the configured-commands story-evidence path wraps that plan result through externalResult() (verifier.ts:977, args type + return object list provider/status/allPass/summary/details/warnings/timestamp/headSha/commands/focus only — no concurrentWorktreePollution field), and the call site at verifier.ts:1318 that builds `result` from `base` (the executeValidationPlan output) does not forward base.concurrentWorktreePollution either. That wrapped `result` is what flows into decorateAndMaybePersistStoryValidation -> persistStoryValidationEvidence, whose evidence() closure at verifier.ts:891-893 checks `result?.concurrentWorktreePollution` to decide whether to pass concurrentPollutionBlocking:true into summarizeRoutineCommandExecution. Since the field never survives the wrap, concurrentPollutionBlocking is never true for the real lattice validate --story=B-xxx --json path, regardless of whether concurrent pollution was actually detected. Reproduced directly against the built dist (two-command concurrent-write fixture, jobs=2): executeValidationPlan returns status=fail with a populated concurrentWorktreePollution.blocking=true, but replaying verifier.ts externalResult()s exact field whitelist plus persistStoryValidationEvidences exact evidence() logic on that output produces a persisted test-evidence.json with result=FAIL (correct, since status/allPass do pass through) but commandExecution={status:PASS, requiredFailureCount:0, complete:true, optionalFailureCount:0} (wrong) -- exactly the shape isReusableCommandPass (validation-evidence-reuse.ts:242-259) checks, and commandExecution is documented at validation-types.ts/types.ts:1710 as project command truth, intentionally independent. Today this happens not to cause an observable reuse bypass only because evaluateRoutineValidationReuse (validation-evidence-reuse.ts:322) ALSO independently checks evidence.result !== PASS, a coincidental second gate, not a designed safety net for this field. This directly contradicts the F-003 commit messages own claim (613bea5432) that the set-attributed record is counted as a required failure by summarizeRoutineCommandExecution (the other gate that reads pollution) so it cannot go silently missing there -- that guarantee holds only when summarizeRoutineCommandExecution is called directly with a hand-supplied flag (as validate-pollution-attribution.test.mjs section 6 does), not when driven through the actual verifier.ts wiring. Fix: thread concurrentWorktreePollution through externalResult() (or pass it separately) at the verifier.ts:1318 call site so persistStoryValidationEvidence sees it, and add a regression that drives the SAME scenario through the real handler/persisted evidence path (not summarizeRoutineCommandExecution called directly) to prevent recurrence.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed in 0d4231e1d1 by making the verifier.ts wrap additive instead of subtractive: const result = { ...base, ...externalResult({...}) }. Every whitelisted key is still computed identically, so the only behavioural delta is that a field the wrapper does not override now survives by construction and a future ValidationResult field cannot be lost by forgetting to list it. Reproduced through the REAL handler before and after (node packages/main/dist/cli.js validate --story=B-f006 --json against a two-command fixture synchronised by a handshake rather than sleeps, so both observation windows provably contain the row on any host): before, persisted evidence read result FAIL but commandExecution status PASS with requiredFailureCount 0; after, commandExecution status FAIL requiredFailureCount 1 and isReusableCommandPass returns false, while the clean control still persists a genuine reusable PASS. Whitelist audit covered all nine externalResult call sites; only the plan path wraps a pre-existing result object and concurrentWorktreePollution was the only drop. Secondary impact also fixed: the drop had stripped the record from evidence.output, which done-oracle and validation-evidence-admissibility parse, so a DONE reader previously saw a FAIL with no stated cause. Regression is section 8 of validate-pollution-attribution.test.mjs (already registered as validate.commands[106]), which calls isReusableCommandPass itself rather than restating its predicate, plus a structural guard comparing handler result keys against a directly-executed plan; the guard was proven to bite by injecting a headSha deletion into the built handler.

.lattice/story/actives/B-7dff/checklist.json:561-572 CHK-005:happy:0 permanent waiver: the compound happy intent requires BOTH declared count materially above 36 AND measured wall time below the 1006s baseline recorded at 36 declarations. Only the first half is demonstrated (declared moved 36->97, VI-OK B7DFF-CHK002-CONFIGURED-PLAN-CLASSIFIED). The waivers own cited number for the second half is 1474.9s at jobs=4 on the final tree (npm run bench:validate-parallel, CHK-004:happy:0 evidence note) -- HIGHER than the 1006s baseline this items userSees explicitly promises to beat, not lower. The waiver text states Substance IS verified and attributes the miss to a mis-specified PLAN pin (absolute cross-session wall clock vs noisy host), citing only the same-session relative speedup (1.51x, CHK-004) as a substitute. That relative number does show parallel beats serial on the CURRENT plan, but it does not show that CHK-005s classification work (36->97 declared) actually reduced wall time below where it stood before this items own work started, which is the specific claim in userSees and the happy verificationIntent. No controlled before/after comparison at matched load exists anywhere in this stories evidence. Recommend either downgrading userSees/verificationIntent to the true measured claim (relative speedup only, not an absolute-baseline reduction) or providing a same-session/matched-load comparison showing declared=97 beats declared=36. As written, the item is marked done on a waiver whose central deliverable claim is contradicted by the stories own only real-plan measurement.
findings.resolvedReason: The finding is accepted as correct and the waiver was rewritten rather than defended. The original note asserted Substance IS verified for the whole compound intent while the intent wall-time clause is contradicted by the story own only real-plan measurement (1474.9s at declared=97 against the 1006s the clause names). The superseding waiver now claims only the declared-count half (36 to 97, proven by the pinned command at HEAD) and states explicitly that the classification effect on wall time is NOT proven: the 1.51x pair is jobs=1 versus jobs=4 both at declared=97, so it demonstrates parallel beats serial and says nothing about 36-declared versus 97-declared. It also records that the missing matched-load comparison was possible (two back-to-back jobs=4 runs in one session) and simply was not run, rather than dressing the omission up as a methodological limit. Marked partially_mitigated, not fixed: the measurement gap the reviewer identified is real and remains open; only the false claim about it has been removed.
